claim:separable-calcium-sparks.proposition: Schaff et al. 2016, Test 1 / Fig 1B: separable calcium sparks on both solvers
claim:separable-calcium-sparks.hypothesis:
The channels' gating is independent of calcium, so E[U] solves the linear PDE driven by
the exact open probability p(t) = k_on/(k_on+k_off)·(1 − e^-(k_on+k_off)t). Both solvers'
trial means converge to it with ε ∝ N^-1/2. At N = 128 the statistical error dominates
the Δt error for Δt ≤ 0.02 s. The two solvers differ only by sampling.

provenance.note: Schaff et al. 2016, Fig 1B; Monte Carlo error ∝ N^-1/2 when statistical error dominates.
Independent ensembles of the same expectation; the ratio is about 1 when only sampling differs.

claim:coupled-sparks-fast-diffusion.proposition: Schaff et al. 2016, Test 2 / Fig 2: coupled calcium sparks in the fast-diffusion limit, both solvers
claim:coupled-sparks-fast-diffusion.hypothesis:
At D = 1000 the cell is effectively well mixed. The spatial hybrid's volume-averaged
U and open count n then follow the well-mixed piecewise-deterministic process, which
the paper sampled with the Gibson–Bruck method; here it is sampled exactly by
event-driven simulation (viva_pde_particle.benchmarks.pdmp).

provenance.note: Fast-diffusion limit; 500 trials against 20,000 exact realizations.
The paper's metric (Fig 2, 10,000 realizations gave about 0.002–0.003). With 500 trials the sampling floor is about 0.05.
The two solvers should agree; 6 comparisons with ties in n make KS conservative.

claim:single-channel-fokker-planck.proposition: Schaff et al. 2016, Tests 3–5 / Figs 4–6: a coupled single channel against direct Fokker–Planck solutions
claim:single-channel-fokker-planck.hypothesis:
The hybrid samples the same piecewise-deterministic process the Fokker–Planck equations
describe, so its histograms should match them to within sampling noise (reduced χ² ≈ 1). The
paper reports L2 differences of 1–3% of the maximum.

provenance.note: Sampling noise alone gives ≈ 1 (the 99th percentile of χ²/k for k ≈ 20–40 bins is about 1.7–1.9).
As above. The paper reports a relative L2 of 1.9% (i = 0) and 3.3% (i = 1).

narrative.question: Do VCell's native PDE/particle hybrid solver (vcell-fvsolver with embedded Smoldyn) and the process-bigraph co-simulation both reproduce the validation results of Schaff et al. (2016, PLoS Comput Biol 12:e1005236), and where do they differ?
